_about: CShapes-Europe records hold the borders as of 1 January of each year (mostly), so a change between two records happened some time before the new record's first year.

Each entry gives the real date of one record boundary that the bank may use as a tell, with a source. 'from' moves the start of the unit's record that begins on 1 January of that year (and ends its previous record the day before); 'to' moves the end of the unit's record that ends on 31 December of that year. 'date' is the first day of the new state.

An entry with 'fill' instead adds a record for that unit from 'from' to 'to', drawn with the shape of another record ('shape': its unit and 1 January start), to cover land that would otherwise be unclaimed between two records.

Only boundaries that match one well-documented event are listed. Boundaries that bundle events from different years (Lombardy 1859 with Tuscany and Nice 1860, coded at 1861) or that could not be matched to a source (several Russo-Ottoman shifts in the Caucasus) are left out, and build-bank.mjs rejects any 1816-1885 puzzle whose tell falls on them.
